forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260324204708_474b5c77
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Assume k is a field, d is a nonnegative integer, and S is the weighted graded polynomial ring on d variables over k with deg(x_i)=w_i where each w_i is a positive integer. For any homogeneous elements g_1,...,g_d in S, if the k-vector space S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d is finite-dimensional, then for each i from 1 to d, the natural image of g_i in the quotient S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_{i-1} is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, the sequence g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence with respect to the same grading.

payload.statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d are homogeneous elements of S and S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k, then for each i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
